correctness.rationale: The displayed Plackett derivative is the bivariate-normal density, integrated via Tonelli against the correlation survival function. Mills quantile expansions yield each fixed-angular endpoint factor. An explicit bound proportional to t^(a-1/2) exp(-t/4) uniformly controls the full moving integration range, completing dominated convergence. Gamma and differentiated inverse-Gaussian integrals provide exact constants, with finite numerical quadrature and a derivative check reproducing 100 assertions. No unsupported inference from finite experiments is made.

value.rationale: For near-asymptotically dependent Gaussian correlation mixtures, the known vanishing first-order tail coefficient and residual exponent one fail to determine practical two-threshold joint risk. The theorem gives a universal endpoint-power classification, exact diagonal Gamma factor, and an explicit non-product off-diagonal logarithmic law (uniform mixing). These are intrinsic and analytically motivated invariants of a natural same-object probability model, not arbitrary substitutions or known-table recomputation.
